key_difference: (D) implements clearLocalData() as an unconditional d.set(nullptr), so calling it during shutdown can re-create thread-local storage with nothing left to destroy it, which is why QGenerationalCollatorHolder's destructor still needs the QThreadData guard. (B) adds QThreadStorageData::clear(), which checks QThreadData::currentThreadData() first, making clearLocalData() always safe in shutdown code and removing the workaround (and the qthread_p.h include) from qcollator.cpp.
